title: Vanishing of Cech H^1 on a cofinal system of coverings gives surjectivity on sections (any site)
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $0\to\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\iota}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal H\to0$ a short exact sequence in the abelian category $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$ and suppose there is a set $\Sigma$ of coverings of $U$ which is cofinal (every covering $\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$ of $U$ is refined by some $\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}\in\Sigma$: for every $t$ there are $j\in J$ and a morphism $U_t\to V_j$ over $U$) and such that $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $\mathcal U\in\Sigma$ (Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]). Then $\varphi_U:\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal H(U)$ is surjective. (General-site version of [lem-weil-pbc-ses-cech-h1-surjective], which is stated for the small etale site and whose proof applies verbatim once 'epimorphism of abelian sheaves = locally surjective' and 'kernels are sectionwise' are available on a general site.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F8 (lemma-ses-cech-h1) and its proof (local lifts of a section of H on a covering, refinement in the cofinal system, the Cech 1-cocycle of differences, correction by a 0-cochain, gluing in G)

proof.text: **Step 1 (what exactness gives).** Write $\iota:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ and $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ for the maps of the sequence. Exactness of $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal H\to0$ in the abelian category $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] means: $\varphi\circ\iota=0$, $\iota$ is a monomorphism, $\varphi$ is an epimorphism, and $\mathrm{Im}(\iota)=\mathrm{Ker}(\varphi)$; so $\iota$ is a kernel of $\varphi$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ (a monomorphism is the kernel of the map to its image's cokernel; here $\mathrm{Im}(\iota)=\mathcal F$ as subobjects of $\mathcal G$). Kernels of abelian sheaves are computed sectionwise: the inclusion $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ preserves limits [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact, part 1], and kernels in $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ are taken objectwise. Hence for every object $V$ of $\mathcal C$ the sequence $0\to\mathcal F(V)\xrightarrow{\iota_V}\mathcal G(V)\xrightarrow{\varphi_V}\mathcal H(V)$ is exact: $\iota_V$ is injective with image $\ker\varphi_V$; in particular $\varphi_V\circ\iota_V=0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F8 (lemma-ses-cech-h1), proof: 'Since s_i lifts s we see that s_{i_0i_1} ∈ F(U_{i_0} ×_U U_{i_1})' (kernel computed sectionwise); literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex Lemma Tag 03CN (lemma-abelian-abelian) part (2)

proof.text: **Step 2 (local lifts).** Let $h\in\mathcal H(U)$. Since $\varphi$ is an epimorphism of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ (Step 1), it is locally surjective [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective]: there are a covering $\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$ of $U$ in $\mathcal C$ and sections $g'_j\in\mathcal G(V_j)$ with $\varphi_{V_j}(g'_j)=h|_{V_j}$ for all $j$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F8 (lemma-ses-cech-h1), proof: 'Since we can certainly find a covering such that (b) holds' (b: s|_{U_i} is the image of a section s_i ∈ G(U_i)); sites-modules.tex Lemma Tag 03CN part (5)

proof.text: **Step 3 (refinement into $\Sigma$).** As $\Sigma$ is cofinal, there is $\mathcal U=\{f_t:U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}\in\Sigma$ refining $\{V_j\to U\}$: for each $t$ choose $j(t)\in J$ and a morphism $a_t:U_t\to V_{j(t)}$ over $U$. Put $g_t=\mathcal G(a_t)(g'_{j(t)})\in\mathcal G(U_t)$. By naturality of $\varphi$ and functoriality of $\mathcal H$ (the composite $U_t\xrightarrow{a_t}V_{j(t)}\to U$ is $f_t$), $\varphi_{U_t}(g_t)=\mathcal H(a_t)(\varphi_{V_{j(t)}}(g'_{j(t)}))=\mathcal H(a_t)(h|_{V_{j(t)}})=h|_{U_t}$. So $\mathcal U$ satisfies (a) $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ (hypothesis on $\Sigma$) and (b) each $h|_{U_t}$ lifts to $g_t$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F8 (lemma-ses-cech-h1), proof: 'Choose a covering U = {U_i → U} such that (a) ... and (b) ... it follows from the assumptions of the lemma that we can find a covering such that (a) and (b) both hold'

proof.text: **Step 4 (the Cech 1-cocycle of differences).** Use the chosen fibre products $U_{t_0t_1}=U_{t_0}\times_UU_{t_1}$, $U_{t_0t_1t_2}$ with projections $\mathrm{pr}_k$ and the face maps $\delta_j^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] (b); write $s|$ for restriction along these. For $(t_0,t_1)\in T^2$ put $\gamma_{t_0t_1}=\mathcal G(\mathrm{pr}_1)(g_{t_1})-\mathcal G(\mathrm{pr}_0)(g_{t_0})\in\mathcal G(U_{t_0t_1})$. Since $f_{t_0}\mathrm{pr}_0=f_{t_1}\mathrm{pr}_1$, Step 3 and naturality give $\varphi(\gamma_{t_0t_1})=h|_{U_{t_0t_1}}-h|_{U_{t_0t_1}}=0$, so by Step 1 there is a unique $c_{t_0t_1}\in\mathcal F(U_{t_0t_1})$ with $\iota(c_{t_0t_1})=\gamma_{t_0t_1}$, and $c=(c_{t_0t_1})\in\check{\mathcal C}^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$. It is a cocycle: with the sign convention of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] (c), $d(c)_{t_0t_1t_2}=\mathcal F(\delta_0^*)(c_{t_1t_2})-\mathcal F(\delta_1^*)(c_{t_0t_2})+\mathcal F(\delta_2^*)(c_{t_0t_1})$ on $U_{t_0t_1t_2}$. Its image under the injective $\iota_{U_{t_0t_1t_2}}$ is, since $\iota$ commutes with restriction and $\mathrm{pr}_k\circ\delta_j^*=\mathrm{pr}_{\delta_j(k)}$, $(g_{t_2}|-g_{t_1}|)-(g_{t_2}|-g_{t_0}|)+(g_{t_1}|-g_{t_0}|)=0$, each $g_{t_k}$ restricted along $\mathrm{pr}_k:U_{t_0t_1t_2}\to U_{t_k}$; hence $d(c)=0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F8 (lemma-ses-cech-h1), proof: 'Consider the sections s_{i_0i_1} = s_{i_1}|_{U_{i_0}×_U U_{i_1}} − s_{i_0}|_{U_{i_0}×_U U_{i_1}}. Since s_i lifts s we see that s_{i_0i_1} ∈ F(U_{i_0}×_U U_{i_1})' (the cocycle identity is left implicit there)

proof.text: **Step 5 (correction by a 0-cochain).** Since $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\ker d^1/\operatorname{im}d^0=0$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] (d), there is $s=(s_t)\in\check{\mathcal C}^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_t\mathcal F(U_t)$ with $c=d(s)$, i.e. $c_{t_0t_1}=\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_1)(s_{t_1})-\mathcal F(\mathrm{pr}_0)(s_{t_0})$ (for $p=0$, $\delta_0^*=\mathrm{pr}_1$, $\delta_1^*=\mathrm{pr}_0$). Put $\tilde g_t=g_t-\iota(s_t)\in\mathcal G(U_t)$. Applying $\iota$ (which commutes with restriction) gives $\mathcal G(\mathrm{pr}_1)(\tilde g_{t_1})=\mathcal G(\mathrm{pr}_0)(\tilde g_{t_0})$ in $\mathcal G(U_{t_0t_1})$ for all $(t_0,t_1)\in T^2$; and $\varphi(\tilde g_t)=\varphi(g_t)-\varphi\iota(s_t)=h|_{U_t}$ since $\varphi\circ\iota=0$ (Step 1).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F8 (lemma-ses-cech-h1), proof: 'By the vanishing of Ȟ^1(U,F) we can find sections t_i ∈ F(U_i) such that s_{i_0i_1} = t_{i_1}| − t_{i_0}|. Then clearly the sections s_i − t_i satisfy the sheaf condition'

proof.text: **Step 6 (gluing).** $\mathcal U$ is a covering of $U$ and $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: $\mathcal G(U)\to\prod_t\mathcal G(U_t)\rightrightarrows\prod_{t_0,t_1}\mathcal G(U_{t_0}\times_UU_{t_1})$ is an equalizer, with the two arrows restriction along the two projections; the condition does not depend on the choice of the fibre products (another choice differs by a unique isomorphism over the projections), so the chosen $U_{t_0t_1}$ may be used. By Step 5 the family $(\tilde g_t)$ lies in the equalizer, so there is $g\in\mathcal G(U)$ with $g|_{U_t}=\tilde g_t$ for all $t$. Then $\varphi_U(g)|_{U_t}=\varphi_{U_t}(\tilde g_t)=h|_{U_t}$ for all $t$, and since $\mathcal H$ is a sheaf, $\mathcal H(U)\to\prod_t\mathcal H(U_t)$ is injective, so $\varphi_U(g)=h$. As $h$ was arbitrary, $\varphi_U$ is surjective.
